args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions, with an error rate of 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to deploy it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The SEV2 for checkout-api is titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0." It explains the failure and the rollback, and it paged the on-call engineer. It also says the root cause needs to be found before anyone tries v2.3.1 again.

The test build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging. Even so, v2.3.1 still went to production, so it's worth checking why the release process didn't stop it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
